name: Rehob
overview: The name Rehob appears in Scripture with several distinct references, reflecting its importance in both people and places. It is identified as the father of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, whom David defeated as he sought to extend his territory (2 Samuel 8:3). Rehob also designates various towns in northern Palestine, including a Levitical city within the territory of Asher that was not fully conquered from the Canaanites (Joshua 19:28, 19:30; Joshua 21:31; Judges 1:31). Additionally, the land reconnaissance by the twelve spies extended up to Rehob, marking a northern boundary in their survey (Numbers 13:21). These references collectively emphasize Rehob’s significance in Israel’s history as both a familial name linked to regional kingship and as a geographical marker within God’s covenant land.
